choices.reason: Diethyl malonate measured only 4.6–5.9/6.3–7.9 mL at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1, far earlier than its prior predictions. This 5/1 point tests whether the revised 7.6/12.6 mL prediction captures the low-ratio edge of that blind spot.

Cyanobenzophenone rose from measured 5.1/21.3 mL at 5/1 to 19.7/55.7 mL at 20/1. The 50/1 prediction is 37.7/90.5 mL; measuring it tests the high-ratio continuation after earlier 5/1 and 10/1 predictions were too late.

This phenylpyridine is predicted at 36.3/70.0 mL at 50/1. Two acquired ring-nitrogen compounds eluted substantially later than predicted, so this tests whether that generalization problem extends to a different heteroaromatic scaffold.

Quinoline measured 27.9/57.7 mL at 5/1 versus a prior prediction of 19.6/41.8 mL. The 10/1 prediction of 28.3/62.8 mL tests whether the model now captures its solvent-ratio response; the pending methylquinoline is a related but distinct molecule.
Dimethylpyridine measured 43.5/118.6 mL at 20/1, far above its prior prediction. This 5/1 prediction of 26.4/63.7 mL starts a matched-condition pair to locate where the strong retention develops.
At matched 150 µL loading, the 10/1 dimethylpyridine prediction is 34.5/92.2 mL. Together with 5/1 and the measured 20/1 point, it tests the shape of a large V2 and elution-width response.

The amino-substituted unsaturated ester measured 47.0/119.4 mL at 20/1, greatly exceeding its prior prediction. A 10/1 measurement probes the lower-ratio response, though its DCM loading conditions differ from the measured PE-loaded point.
For this multifunctional ester, measured V2 rose from 43.9 mL at 5/1 to 94.2 mL at 10/1 and was underpredicted at both. The 2/1 prediction of 9.6/21.3 mL tests where the sharp change begins.

The 5/1 aminobenzonitrile prediction is 19.7/45.7 mL. An acquired aminoacetophenone was later than predicted, but the structures and conditions differ; this is a weak test of transfer to another amine-bearing aromatic molecule.

The phenolic aldehyde measured 22.9/57.5 mL at 50/1 and was predicted fairly closely. Its 0/1 prediction of 4.4/20.2 mL tests whether V2 remains broad under strong eluent, without assuming the errors seen for other phenols apply here.

A related bromohydroxybenzaldehyde was earlier than predicted at 20/1. This 0/1 candidate probes the strong-eluent endpoint, but bromine position and loading volume also differ, so the comparison is weak.

The 2/1 trimethoxybenzene prediction is 12.7/25.8 mL. Paired with the pending 5/1 experiment on the same molecule, it tests whether the model transfers the solvent-ratio effect to a methoxy-rich aromatic; direct measured evidence is absent.

This 20/1 o-tolunitrile prediction of 16.5/26.8 mL bridges to its pending 50/1 experiment. Cyanobenzophenone was overpredicted at 5/1 and 10/1, but that different scaffold provides only weak evidence for a nitrile-wide issue.

The 1/1 cyclopropyl β-ketoester prediction is 4.1/8.4 mL. It supplies a strong-eluent anchor for the pending 20/1 experiment on the same molecule and tests whether the large predicted ratio contrast is real.
This bromomethyl benzoate measured 5.4/11.5 mL at 1/1 and 7.0/16.5 mL at 5/1. The 50/1 prediction of 20.2/36.7 mL tests extrapolation of its observed rising response to a PE-rich condition.

The benzyl-substituted β-ketoester is predicted at 23.8/42.1 mL at 20/1. Measurements on a simpler β-ketoester cover only 2/1 and 5/1, so this weak chemical-transfer probe tests the effect of substitution at high PE.

hypotheses.content: The earlier prediction that diethyl malonate becomes much later from 10/1 to 20/1 is contradicted: measured V1/V2 are 5.9/7.5 mL at 10/1, 4.6/6.3 mL at 20/1 and 5.8/7.9 mL at 50/1. These are far earlier than premeasurement predictions; behavior of phenyl-substituted malonate does not transfer directly.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 5/1 measurement also remain early, or is there a change below 10/1?

hypotheses.content: The proposed local fluorobenzoate V2 reversal was observed at matched 100 µL loading: V2 is 12.71 mL at 5/1 and 12.31 mL at 10/1. The 0.40 mL difference is small, so the shape should not be generalized confidently; V1 increased over the same contrast.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the small V2 reversal persist across another loading amount or replicate?

hypotheses.content: The earlier high-ratio plateau hypothesis for methyl benzoylformate is contradicted. V2 measured 33.3 mL at 20/1 and 62.0 mL at 50/1, while premeasurement predictions stayed near 29 mL; the high-ratio elution width was substantially underpredicted.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where between 20/1 and 50/1 does the large rise in V2 occur?

hypotheses.content: The earlier anthranilate solvent-ratio-rise hypothesis is supported: measured V1/V2 progress from about 9/17 mL at 5/1 to 13.5/26.0 at 10/1, 19.9/38.2 at 20/1 and 34.0/75.2 at 50/1. The 10/1 prediction was close, while the 50/1 prediction underestimated both endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a related anthranilate show the same additional high-ratio rise?

hypotheses.content: Cyanobenzophenone shows a measured rise from 3.6/8.9 mL at 0/1 to 19.7/55.7 mL at 20/1, supporting a solvent-strength effect. Its premeasurement predictions were too late at 5/1 and 10/1, so the model misplaced part of the response curve; the 50/1 outcome remains unknown.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does measured V1/V2 at 50/1 approach the current 37.7/90.5 mL prediction?

hypotheses.content: Nitroacetophenone directly supports a large solvent-ratio response: measured V1/V2 change from 3.9/11.7 mL at 0/1 to 25.6/55.1 mL at 10/1. The 10/1 premeasurement V2 prediction of 66.8 mL was too late, so the magnitude remains a model issue.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At an intermediate ratio, does V2 rise smoothly or sharply?

hypotheses.content: Some aromatic ring-nitrogen compounds were later and wider than predicted: quinoline measured 27.9/57.7 mL at 5/1 and dimethylpyridine 43.5/118.6 mL at 20/1. This is not universal across nitrogen-containing molecules: ethyl nicotinate V2 was overpredicted at 2/1. Structural context and solvent ratio may matter.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched ratio series on quinoline and dimethylpyridine preserve the underpredicted late elution, and does phenylpyridine behave similarly?

hypotheses.content: At PE-rich conditions, V2 was substantially underpredicted for the measured multifunctional ester at 5/1 and 10/1 and for the amino-substituted unsaturated ester at 20/1. A shared mechanism is unproven; the observations justify probing lower ratios on each molecule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1 for the multifunctional ester and 10/1 for the amino ester, where does measured V2 begin to diverge from predictions?

hypotheses.content: Two PE-rich phenols had large V2 underpredictions: trifluoromethoxyphenol measured 85.6 versus predicted 47.3 mL, and iodophenol measured 97.9 versus predicted 48.5 mL. The phenolic aldehyde at 50/1 was predicted closely, so this is a subset-specific observation rather than a general phenol rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do phenolic aldehydes behave under strong eluent, and do their widths remain large?

hypotheses.content: β-Ketoester structure and solvent ratio may jointly affect elution. The simple ethyl acetoacetate measurements give 9.0/20.2 mL at 2/1 and 11.4/25.3 mL at 5/1, but they cannot establish the response of cyclopropyl or benzyl-substituted variants at the selected conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do the cyclopropyl compound's 1/1 and pending 20/1 outcomes compare, and is the benzyl-substituted 20/1 result distinct?

hypotheses.content: Bromomethyl benzoate V1/V2 increase from measured 5.4/11.5 mL at 1/1 to 7.0/16.5 mL at 5/1. Extrapolation to 50/1 is an untested model inference; the two observed points establish only the low-ratio direction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, does measured V1/V2 approach the predicted 20.2/36.7 mL?

result.feedback_interpretation: The revealed batch redirected this search toward specific failures: diethyl malonate stayed early despite very late predictions; methyl benzoylformate, multifunctional esters, selected phenols and ring-nitrogen compounds showed large V2 errors; cyanobenzophenone's predicted ratio curve was too late at 5/1 and 10/1. I chose lower-ratio anchors, matched-condition bridges and one higher-ratio extrapolation for those patterns. Anthranilate's 10/1 and 20/1 results were comparatively well predicted, so I did not spend another choice on it.
